title: I have a lambda
content:
The inevitable happened. We're even counting the years since. We're in calm waters, not a single wave in the sea. But... at least one of you would swim towards me ;_;

I tripled my carbon footprint overnight.
Imagine a future where you can actually get cold in winter. Your friends invite you out, and you have to wear a coat. You never, ever take a minibus. Istanbul's public transport card doesn't require ID verification. Everyone you meet looks amazing. You get together once a week to play D&D 3.5, and the whole world hates everything new along with you. Dreaming is free, after all.
It's rare for me to run out of things to say. When it comes to rambling on, nobody's better than me. But lately, I've been surrounded by some pretty stupid people. People whose lack of understanding isn't evident in their answers, but in their faces. If they were trying, great. But they give up from the start.
I've stopped expecting anyone to teach me anything; I can't teach anyone myself. Years of accumulated knowledge are gathering dust on a bookshelf, like a Turkish book whose origin is unknown. I really want to be useful. Whatever happens, I want my existence to lead to something.

My crimes always went unpunished; I wish you could have taken some of them with you.
I'd understand if they didn't like me. They're so eager to see me. But when we sit across from each other, they just listen in silence. I don't know, I don't really remember what it used to be, but it seems like things used to be more interactive. When I ask a question, they just stare at me and freeze. I have to say ten sentences just to get one from them. And the answers I get seem to come from somewhere memorized.
I find myself explaining very simple things at length, for example. It spoils my enjoyment.
When I talk to someone, it's like we're showing each other picture cards. Whatever the word evokes, that's what it is. If I say something a little complicated, I regret it. If I knew better, I wouldn't lift my head from my games. Why am I paying the price for their ignorance?

I will sleep when I die.
"You're with the wrong people." Are there even any people left?
I barely have a handful, and I tolerate them by making huge compromises. Their words and actions don't match, and they can't even spend two minutes brainstorming. I'm so fed up with people. I don't understand how they manage to agree with the rest of the world on everything. At least try to add some color to the conversation. Let's explore a couple of hypothetical scenarios together. But no, they're boring even in their fantasies.
I read somewhere that people with below-average IQs can't grasp hypothetical scenarios very well. They can't go beyond the scenario, even in their fantasies. I wish we saw this consistency in more important matters.
I tried to sabotage my life for a long time because I was so bored. Literally everything I did backfired. I kept doing what I was doing, and they kept praising me. I guess they don't even understand what I'm saying; they judge my actions by the air I give off. If I acted even slightly shy, they'd walk all over me.

I'm quadrupling my carbon footprint!
I'm trying to be positive now; maybe it really isn't my fault. Maybe I'm paying the price for being a shitty person, not for reading too many books in high school.
Still, let's be realistic. Even if I were playing a different role, it still leads to the same place. It's not a cultural divide, because I don't have that kind of intellectual side. I just want a reason to step outside the house. How can there really be nothing to do in this huge city of Istanbul? How can all the activities consist of sitting in a place and drinking? I went to places that are supposed to be teeming with nerds a few times. Even there, I didn't hear anything new. It's like someone pressed the stop button on the world and flushed it.

We need to kiss sometimes too.
I don't know if it's just me, but conversations don't last long anymore unless you're actively trying to hook up with someone. To play an MMORPG with someone and have a voice call, I have to trick them with my dick. I even had to build a harem just to play D&D.
I don't know. My expectations were so different. I thought new things would test me, challenge me a bit. Life would get more complicated, and so on. Instead, I've faced a huge drop in quality. It's like there's no material left; I'm just stuck with cheap repetitions. I can't even find solace in hedonism anymore.

We've whined enough.
Thank you for reading my personal blog.

title: things stolen from me
content:
Let's cut down this huge tree and count the rings inside.

Let's cut down this huge tree and count the rings inside.
I need to talk a little about things I got away with. After all, I have a Legacy to keep alive. Otherwise, what difference would there be between me and you?
There's no need to start from the beginning of time. I'll continue from where I left off so that no one gets confused.
I categorize the players in my life according to their ability to dominate their surroundings. I carefully observe how lasting their words and actions are, and how much they deviate from the course our world is following. If this deviation remains below three degrees, I can overlook it based on certain invisible constants.

I'll start with my first victim.
I never attempted to burden myself with the mission of a prophet. The path I try to follow in my life is more like that of a dervish. Time and space are no longer relevant. There is no destination. Whoever wants something from me takes it, but dervishes carry axes. They carry these axes so that if a wild animal appears before them, they can strike it on the head. In short, I may be aimless, but I am still sharp-witted.
Sometimes, instead of an animal, a tree appears before me. This tree asks me to prune it. Although I don't want to waste my axe like this, I can't refuse it. I start with the drooping branches, and when those branches recede and clear my path, I prune the rotten branches. These branches, shaped by the strong winds the tree withstands, wrap around the tree's trunk. They surround it like armor. Because I can't wield the axe skillfully, sometimes I miss the branches and wound the tree itself.
Actually, this is the job of a gardener. But this creature in need of help can only be found by me because I stray from the path and delve into the bushes. I know that if I'm not the one to prune it, nobody else will.

If a tree falls by itself in a deserted forest...
I thought repetition was my curse. Things we inherited from Sisyphus. No, repetition was a warning. Repetition is the point where the unstoppable force strikes that object, which is perfectly manageable and will never move. Someone important once said; You go around the wall, I get up every time I fall and run back to it until I knock the wall down with my head. That man, one day, decided to walk around the wall, but for some reason, he put me in its place. Here, rather than Sisyphus, we became Heracles, bearing the weight of Atlas.
You can't move anywhere when you have the weight of the whole world on your shoulders. You understand. Now that we've vomited out cheap symbolism from our system, let's get to the point. The burden I carried was my loved ones, who would never learn. They hadn't come into existence on their own; their parents had created them. They were helpless against them. They either became like them or walked the path they had drawn. In return, I stood by the side of the road, waving to them. They really wanted to come to me. But for that, they needed to think for themselves, to leave their comfort zones.
As I showed some of them the path to freedom, the increasing risk made them more cowardly. They became so cowardly that the first thing they took refuge in was the system society had already imposed on them. Like a child who falls off a bicycle and hesitates to ride it again, the fault wasn't in their own incompetence, but in the methods. And who knows how many times I fell before I could prove that these methods worked.
It wasn't my cult leader charisma that inspired them. It was my approachability. I hadn't descended from the top of a special caste system. In fact, I was right on the ground. My story wasn't a success story. It was a harbinger of a happy ending that could be reached at some point. We hadn't reached it yet, but we were very close.

Ta-da! Actually, there was a spoon, I just wasn't sharing it with you.
My disgust is directed at those who are afraid to live. Because they are the ones who most often break their own rules. Because they offer everything that pertains to them to be broken. To be broken by masters, to be broken for alms, to be broken so that they feel good.
This fear stems from a refusal to accept. But this is not a virtue. All that needs to be done is for a person to accept that they are without virtue, without honor, without backbone. Everything that makes us feel like we have character is a fabrication. It makes us invisible to the weapons of society. Conformists are blind, because an unstimulated sense dulls. If one day they stumble, they won't even realize that the power punishing them is the very weapons they have become blind to. The logic of causality is lost. If a person is also foolish, the only resource they can turn to is their own inner world. Delirium begins here. The foundation is already rotten, and every system built on that foundation is crooked.
Faith speaks much of the soul. Yet, it is unknown whether the soul was always immortal.
Humanity should live in the present moment. Not in the afterlife, in imagination, or in assumptions. But we could never make peace with ourselves. We could never accept who we were. Because of our ignorance stemming from our inability to understand the world, all we could decide about what we would become was what they allowed us to be.

Let everyone change their name to Damkina.
I always tried to create a safe space for the people around me. A place where they could be themselves and wouldn't be judged. I simply directed my corners toward the drinks and food they brought from outside. As long as they didn't annoy me, they all got what they wanted.
They thought they deserved it. Yet, behind all this were the struggles I endured. That's what made them special; the fact that they were deemed worthy in my eyes was my sacrifice. But like someone from Istanbul eating a good Iskender kebab for the first time, they thought they could come back here and eat the same kebab again. Life isn't fair. At this point, they will only carry the delusion of an incomplete teaching. Because no one will take them to the right Iskender kebab place, and they will be too shy to ask me.

A bird that flies out of the nest is caught by a cat. Ham.
That's all I could do. I didn't manage to do it right. Some snakes should have their heads crushed early, damn it, I'm a die-hard animal lover. Maybe I don't touch every cat I see and I often have to swing a stick at monkeys, but I sincerely hope you all arrive at your destinations safe and sound.
Singularity, after all, is only granted to freethinkers.

title: If I come to my senses
content:
My mind is in turmoil. The medication I'm taking is having an unwanted effect on me. I'm in conflict with my lifestyle because of it. The source of all my problems is people. This isn't some hard-to-understand secret. When I take the medication, I feel restless and I want to talk. To talk a lot.

Ice-cold, low-calorie energy drinks are my real medicine.
I apologize to all of you for my cryptic introductory posts. I made an explanation for this kind of thing in my previous blog. Normally, I would limit these kinds of vague, nonsensical things to a paragraph or two at the beginning of my posts. This time, it completely overwhelmed me. I haven't written in a long time, that's why I say so.
For those reading my blog for the first time, let me quote from my previous post:
"Among the advice given to writers, there's a saying, 'get rid of the first thousand bad words.' When I talk about the stew I ate and my dream, I'm actually trying to do that a little bit. I need to cleanse myself by draining the bad blood from my system.
Because they poisoned me very badly, my friend, very badly."
I used to keep my blog to myself. Like a diary, I didn't share it with anyone. Whoever found it, found it somehow. Of course, things changed, and later I started sharing, even dragging people into this hobby. Anyway, I never paid attention to what I wrote. But as I heard the comments of those who read my blog, I realized that I was actually creating something interesting, whether I knew it or not.
My nonsensical introductions or extremely vague ramblings. I used to think that someone reading these wouldn't understand them or find them relatable. But apparently, for some people, it's even more valuable. I manage to stimulate their minds without explaining anything. I enjoy hearing things like that.

My cats love the taste the most.
I played Minecraft all night. Finally, I overcame a conditioning that had been holding my mind captive. I couldn't play alone. It's a social game, after all, so naturally, the idea that "This should be played with other people" was ingrained in my mind. I continued until my eyes started to close from sleepiness. I shut off my thoughts and immersed myself in the digital Lego world. The reason I stopped playing was that when I tried to program something impossible with redstone, the gears in my brain started turning again.
I'm good at art. But for a long time – an extremely long time – I haven't been able to create anything new. I can't blame myself, though. I've thought about this a lot and I have some theories.
Art feeds on experience. And I'm not experiencing very interesting things anymore. As a hikikomori, my life is essentially what I experience in my room. All my material comes from the past, but as the years pass, I've naturally become estranged from my memories.
When I look at them, all the works that interest and inspire me share certain common characteristics. Of course they will, but I'm talking about the creative processes here. They never, ever create what they write or draw alone. The creative process takes precedence over the planned story and what will be told. Manga, for example, go through a strong editorial process. A mangaka doesn't do everything alone; they work with a team. While drawing a new chapter each month, the events of that month, the readers' thoughts, and the artist's own self-criticism are all interwoven into the work. I can tell that the dialogues I read weren't written by a man sitting in front of a blank sheet of paper. Yes, I know, these aren't deeply hidden, private pieces of information; I haven't just recently realized this. But lately, I've gained a new perspective and reassembled the pieces.
Most artists aren't satisfied with their work. We can see this especially at the beginning of stories. The form they take according to the industry, the rules they follow in order to create their art, the publishers' demands, the market... Only when they are "successful" do they break free from this and truly express their feelings as they are. The Alien series was the first thing that put this idea in my head.
Film trilogies have a common thread. The FNAF film adaptation, for example, isn't a game series I normally follow. But people are curious about such products of internet culture. I went to see it in theaters because Josh Hutchinson, an actor I like, was in the lead role. The first film was quite weak; perhaps because of the genre, I could see that the production's decisions were quite commercially oriented. Therefore, I didn't approach it critically at all. When I went to see the second film, I realized it was consistent with the theory I'd formed after watching the Alien series. This time, the film was fuller, more entertaining, and more free-flowing. I'm eagerly awaiting the third film.
My theory is this: The first film is always about numbers. It uses formulas strictly to reach as many people as possible and be easily understood. It avoids upsetting the audience. The second film is the real film; the success of the first reveals what they originally intended to do. Once the directors see that the film has already established itself in the audience, and with audience feedback, they begin to open up space for the artists. And that's how the third film happens. There are no longer any boundaries; the mainstream audience might not like it, but the final blow to the series' cult status is struck here. You can analyze any trilogy in this way. Back to the Future's focus on cowboys is entirely an American cinematic metaphor; Alien 3 – if you watch the uncensored director's cut – presents the metaphors the series originally intended to explore in an experimental way. Even in Marvel films I don't particularly like, I've seen the same themes in the Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy and End Game. End Game, in particular, literally transported me into the writers' room. It offered a beautiful critique of clichés and genre conventions. Each character was developed in a way that was seamlessly integrated with their actors. Now they could gain weight, retire, or even pursue stale, easy solutions like time travel without fear or justification.

What saddens me is that I'll never be a part of something like this.
There's a great documentary about how South Park was made. You can watch it on YouTube or something. I highly recommend it. Knowing that people like them exist is really important if you're an artist. Especially after what they did in their later seasons, they broke the bar they were constantly raising. I always see a prejudice against these kinds of series. After all, Rick & Morty has established itself in culture because of its fanbase. Anyway, the reason I'm mentioning this is because you've probably heard why the guys who make Black Mirror don't release new episodes. They say, "What can we do? Everything we've made has become real, are we going to film what's already there?"
South Park is like that too; people keep saying, "Our reality is already a South Park episode." It's always been like that. They're creative comedians, after all, they always manage to twist and turn things and grab hold of them from somewhere. Even though they're quite direct, they hide the subject matter behind a veil of "fiction." Matt and Trey, if you follow them, know that they're extremely dissatisfied with the state of the world. South Park is their call to action for people. But after making twenty seasons of a show, even they can't escape the thought, "South Park is like that." Therefore, the way the final season, which began as if hiding behind layers of fiction, gradually lifted those veils, and the moment the character in question appeared on screen, the complete disbelief built on reality was shattered, was a historic moment.
Fanboyism aside, seeing this triggered a long introspection within myself. My trilogy theory, the whip that South Park lashed at my neck, finally made me realize why everything I did felt so repulsive to me.

My dreams are writing stories for me now.
Artist crises used to be a topic I actively discussed in art communities and fine arts circles. There was something that always bothered me, something that constantly recurred. Leaving aside those who had already established themselves as artists, the others I encountered, amateurs and those just starting out, were always obsessed with how to market their art before even beginning. Strategizing is certainly good, but I don't think I need to explain how harmful it can be for the individual. Even though I consider myself someone who has overcome this, I realized there's another dimension to it.
What influenced me was comics, especially manga. I want to draw manga, I still desperately want to. Yet, what always held me back from starting a proper series was this format, shaped by marketing. The product's constraints. Yes, if you're going to draw manga, you have to follow a certain page format, story structure rules, and visual storytelling techniques. But this is a format entirely shaped by marketing. And it's incredibly restrictive.
I'm working on this these days. I'm reviewing alternatives. And so the idea of making a Visual Novel started to look really appealing.

Of course, things like that take a lot of time.
If I manage to overcome my depression – and I have some things to take care of – I'd like to talk a little bit about my work on Visual Novels. Wish me luck. And of course, if you're interested, you can reach me at the email address on the homepage.
Again, thank you for reading my personal blog.
